s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent painful skin lesions with ulceration and systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Painful pimple-like bumps on bilateral lower legs
Ulcers with central eschars and dusky gray borders
key_facts: Patient is a young black woman
Presented with chills and bilateral lower extremity swelling
Recent course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus
Medical history includes treatment with methimazole and atenolol
Laboratory tests show elevated CRP and ESR
Normal C3 and C4 complement levels
ANA titer 1:80
P-ANCA titer 1:20
Anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) titer 141 U
Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies level 120 U
Punch biopsy shows mid- and deep dermal lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils and focal abscess
Second biopsy shows intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with necrosis of vessel walls

differentials: STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy
Chronic atypical neutrophilic dermatosis with lipodystrophy and elevated temperature
per_call: STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy
Chronic atypical neutrophilic dermatosis with lipodystrophy and elevated temperature

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CRP and ESR, positive P-ANCA and anti-myeloperoxidase titers, and histopathological findings of necrotizing vasculitis

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of purpura, ulcers, and histopathological findings of neutrophilic infiltrate and fibrinoid necrosis

shortlist.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammation, elevated CRP and ESR, and histopathological findings of necrotizing vasculitis

shortlist.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CRP and ESR, positive P-ANCA and anti-myeloperoxidase titers, and histopathological findings of necrotizing vasculitis

shortlist.label: Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of purpura, ulcers, and histopathological findings of neutrophilic infiltrate and fibrinoid necrosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with painful lesions, chills, and bilateral lower extremity swelling, along with laboratory tests showing elevated CRP and ESR, and biopsy results revealing intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with necrosis of vessel walls, are consistent with cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis. The presence of anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) titer and anti-SSA/Ro antibodies also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: Lack of granulomatous inflammation on biopsy

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: While the biopsy shows perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate, the clinical presentation and laboratory results are more consistent with cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis

rejected.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
rejected.why: No evidence of medium-sized artery involvement

rejected.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated MPO titer, the clinical presentation and biopsy results are more consistent with cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
